title.ja: Lambda Managed Instances: Lambda を自分の EC2 キャパシティで動かす
title.en: Lambda Managed Instances: Lambda on EC2 Capacity You Choose

sources.title: Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Lambda Managed Instances runs Lambda functions on current-generation EC2 instances in your account without you managing instance lifecycles, OS and runtime patching, routing, load balancing, or scaling policies
Capacity providers are the foundation: create a capacity provider, create a function attached to it, publish a function version
When a function version is published with a capacity provider, Lambda launches three instances by default for AZ resiliency and starts three execution environments before marking the version ACTIVE
One execution environment handles multiple invocations at the same time; Lambda (default) runs at most one invocation per execution environment
Managed Instances use containers on EC2 Nitro instances for isolation rather than Firecracker; the capacity provider is the security boundary

The instances are EC2 managed instances: the Operator field appears in DescribeInstances, they carry the aws:lambda:capacity-provider tag, they cannot be terminated directly, and they are hidden from the EC2 console and list operations by default while remaining billable
Pricing is EC2-based with a 15% management fee on top of the EC2 instance cost; EC2 Savings Plans, Reserved Instances and other EC2 discounts apply to the EC2 compute only, not to the management fee

Lambda Managed Instances scales asynchronously on CPU resource utilization, without cold starts, and scales to the configured minimum of execution environments without traffic; Lambda (default) scales to zero
By default Managed Instances scale to handle traffic doubling within five minutes

sources.title: Core concepts
supports: All functions assigned to the same capacity provider must be mutually trusted
If traffic more than doubles within 5 minutes, throttles may occur while Lambda scales up
Users need lambda:PassCapacityProvider to assign functions to a capacity provider

sources.title: Capacity providers
supports: A capacity provider takes a VPC configuration (1 to 16 subnets, security groups), an operator role, and optionally instance requirements and a scaling configuration
Architectures is x86_64 or arm64, default x86_64; AllowedInstanceTypes and ExcludedInstanceTypes are mutually exclusive
Lambda chooses instance types by default, and restricting them might result in lower availability
MaxVCpuCount defaults to 400; ScalingMode is Auto or Manual
KmsKeyArn is a KMS key for EBS encryption, defaulting to an AWS managed key
A capacity provider that has function versions attached cannot be deleted
States: Pending, Active, Failed, Deleting

sources.title: Scaling Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Managed Instances does not scale when invocations arrive and does not support cold starts; it scales asynchronously on CPU utilization and multi-concurrency saturation
The smallest supported function size is 2 GB and 1 vCPU
Maximum concurrency per execution environment can be raised to 64 per vCPU
The default minimum is 3 execution environments across Availability Zones with no default maximum; values below 3 reduce Availability Zone redundancy
MinExecutionEnvironments and MaxExecutionEnvironments range from 0 to 15000 and are set together; a minimum of 0 is valid only when the maximum is also 0, which deactivates the function version
A deactivated function does not scale back up with traffic; Lambda terminates an instance once it has no active execution environments, and instance charges continue until termination completes
The Router and Scaler are shared Lambda components; a Lambda Agent runs on each instance
The default target keeps enough headroom for traffic to double within 5 minutes without throttles
For testing or development you might choose smaller instance types

sources.title: Lambda Managed Instances runtimes
supports: Supported: Java 21 and later, Python 3.13 and later, Node.js 22 and later, .NET 8 and later, and Rust on the OS-only runtime provided.al2023 and later
Node.js uses worker threads with asynchronous execution; Python uses one process per concurrent request; Java uses OS threads

sources.title: Node.js runtime for Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Function initialization occurs once per worker thread; concurrent requests on the same worker thread share the handler object and global state
For Node.js the default maximum is 64 concurrent requests per vCPU; the number of worker threads follows the vCPU count or AWS_LAMBDA_NODEJS_WORKER_COUNT
For mutable objects, avoid global state or use AsyncLocalStorage; AWS SDK clients are async safe
On Node.js 22, callback-based handlers cannot be used with Managed Instances
/tmp is shared across all concurrent requests in the execution environment
Functions on Managed Instances always use the structured JSON log format, which carries the requestId
context.awsRequestId and context.xRayTraceId are async-safe; the _X_AMZN_TRACE_ID environment variable is not supported
process.on() cannot be used with worker threads, so a function cannot subscribe to SIGTERM
Minimum versions: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 3.933.0, Powertools for AWS Lambda (TypeScript) 2.29.0

sources.title: Networking for Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Connectivity is needed for functions to reach resources outside the VPC and for transmitting telemetry to CloudWatch Logs and X-Ray
Three options: public subnet with an internet gateway, VPC endpoints, private subnet with a NAT gateway
VPC endpoints are recommended for production with strict security requirements and are billed per endpoint, per Availability Zone, and per GB

sources.title: Security and permissions
supports: Containers are not a security boundary between functions on a capacity provider
lambda:PassCapacityProvider is required when creating or updating functions that use a capacity provider, including through infrastructure as code
Lambda uses the AWSServiceRoleForLambda service-linked role to manage the EC2 resources of capacity providers

sources.title: Lambda operator role for Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Lambda assumes the operator role to manage EC2 instances in the capacity provider; its trust policy names lambda.amazonaws.com

The role needs at least the AWSLambdaManagedEC2ResourceOperator managed policy; the page prints its statements (ec2:RunInstances, ec2:CreateTags, ec2:AttachNetworkInterface, ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, several ec2:Describe*, logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, logs:PutLogEvents)
The service-linked role is created with the first capacity provider, needs iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole for lambda.amazonaws.com, and holds ec2:TerminateInstances and ec2:DescribeInstances

sources.title: Lambda Managed Instances quotas
supports: 1,000 capacity providers per account; 100 function versions per capacity provider (cannot be increased); 15,000 vCPUs per capacity provider
Capacity provider APIs: 15 read requests and 1 write request per second, not adjustable
EC2 quotas apply as well: vCPU limits, EBS volume limits, and free IP addresses in the subnets
Event source mappings on Managed Instances support SQS, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon MSK, and self-managed Apache Kafka

sources.title: Understanding the Lambda Managed Instances execution environment
supports: The execution environment stays active between invocations instead of being frozen
The configured timeout applies to each invocation; when one times out Lambda reports it failed but does not stop the code, which keeps running and keeps a runtime worker busy
If all runtime workers are busy, new invocations are rejected until one is free
Initialization may take up to the larger of 130 seconds and the function timeout
Unhealthy containers are terminated and replaced rather than reset

sources.title: $LATEST.PUBLISHED version in Lambda Managed Instances
supports: An unqualified ARN of a Managed Instances function invokes $LATEST.PUBLISHED, not $LATEST
CloudFormation and the console create the $LATEST.PUBLISHED version automatically

sources.title: Getting started with Lambda Managed Instances
supports: A function is attached with --capacity-provider-config LambdaManagedInstancesCapacityProviderConfig={CapacityProviderArn=...}, and a version must be published before it runs
Cleanup deletes the function first, then the capacity provider
Function creation typically takes several minutes

sources.title: Troubleshooting Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Throttles are HTTP 429; the throttle reason metrics tell CPU, memory, disk and concurrency apart
Node.js state isolation issues: global variables are shared across concurrent invocations on the same worker thread
Missing logs are a VPC connectivity problem: the instances need a path to CloudWatch Logs, for example the com.amazonaws.<region>.logs interface endpoint with private DNS
A function version stays pending while Lambda launches three instances and starts three execution environments; this typically takes several minutes
Metrics are in the AWS/Lambda namespace with the dimensions CapacityProviderName, FunctionName, or InstanceType

sources.title: Lambda quotas
supports: On Managed Instances, asynchronous and event source mapping invocations may run up to 5,400 seconds (90 minutes); the general function timeout is 900 seconds
Managed Instances use a file descriptor limit of 4,096 and the process and thread limits of Bottlerocket

sources.title: Introducing AWS Lambda Managed Instances: Serverless simplicity with EC2 flexibility (AWS News Blog, 2025-11-30)
supports: At launch the feature was available in US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland)
New instances are launched within tens of seconds; by default a capacity provider absorbs spikes of up to 50% without scaling, and throttles with 429 beyond what is provisioned
Instances have a maximum lifetime of 14 days
sources.note: The blog says a 50% spike is absorbed without scaling; the developer guide says capacity is kept for traffic doubling within five minutes. The chapter quotes both and treats neither as measured.

sources.title: AWS Lambda pricing: Lambda Managed Instances
supports: Three components: USD 0.20 per million requests, a compute management fee of 15% of the EC2 On-Demand price, and standard EC2 instance charges
Compute Savings Plans, EC2 Instance Savings Plans and Reserved Instances reduce the EC2 instance charges
Functions on Managed Instances do not pay for the execution duration of each request
Worked example: 100 million requests, m7g.xlarge at USD 0.1632 per hour in us-east-1, a 3-year Compute Savings Plan at 72% off, about 2,000 instance-hours: 20 + 91.40 + 48.96 = USD 160.36
sources.note: The page does not say whether the Lambda free tier covers Managed Instances requests, and does not mention the EBS volumes of the instances.

sources.title: AWS Price List: AWSLambda, ap-northeast-1 (published 2026-10-09)
supports: APN1-Lambda-Managed-Instances-m6g.large-Management-Hours is USD 0.01485 per hour; m7g.large is USD 0.01581 per hour
APN1-Lambda-Managed-Instances-Request-ARM is USD 0.0000002 per request, the same as APN1-Request-ARM
493 instance types have a management fee in ap-northeast-1; the smallest size listed is large, and no c-family large type is listed
The same offer for 30 Regions lists Managed Instances usage types; ap-southeast-6, il-central-1, me-central-1, me-south-1 and the two GovCloud Regions do not
sources.note: Read through region_index.json, one file per Region, counting usage types that contain Lambda-Managed-Instances-. A price being published is not the same statement as the feature being offered; the chapter says which of the two it read.

sources.title: AWS::Lambda::CapacityProvider
supports: Properties: CapacityProviderName, CapacityProviderScalingConfig, InstanceRequirements, KmsKeyArn, PermissionsConfig (required), PropagateTags, Tags, TelemetryConfig, VpcConfig (required)
Changing VpcConfig, PermissionsConfig, InstanceRequirements, KmsKeyArn, or the name replaces the capacity provider

sources.title: AWS::Lambda::Function LambdaManagedInstancesCapacityProviderConfig
supports: CapacityProviderArn is required; ExecutionEnvironmentMemoryGiBPerVCpu ranges from 2 to 8; PerExecutionEnvironmentMaxConcurrency ranges from 1 to 1600

sources.title: CreateCapacityProvider
supports: The API operation is CreateCapacityProvider; its request carries VpcConfig, PermissionsConfig, InstanceRequirements, and CapacityProviderScalingConfig

sources.title: CreateFunction
supports: CreateFunction takes CapacityProviderConfig and PublishTo, whose only valid value is LATEST_PUBLISHED

sources.title: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0: aws-lambda/lib/capacity-provider.d.ts and its JavaScript
supports: lambda.CapacityProvider is an L2 construct with subnets, securityGroups, operatorRole, architectures, instanceTypeFilter, maxVCpuCount, scalingOptions, kmsKey, propagateTags, logGroup
addFunction(func, options) sets CapacityProviderConfig and FunctionScalingConfig on the function
The construct refuses a maxVCpuCount outside 12 to 15000
When operatorRole is omitted the construct creates a role with AWSLambdaManagedEC2ResourceOperator
sources.note: The type comment on perExecutionEnvironmentMaxConcurrency says the default maximum is 10, while the developer guide gives 64 per vCPU as the Node.js default. The stack does not set it, and the chapter quotes the guide.

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28: the installed package's dist
supports: The provider registry registers AWS::Lambda::Function and AWS::Lambda::Permission and has no entry for AWS::Lambda::CapacityProvider, which therefore goes through Cloud Control API

The property coverage of AWS::Lambda::Function lists CapacityProviderConfig and FunctionScalingConfig as 'not yet implemented by cdkd'; a function that has them is routed through Cloud Control API instead of the SDK provider
PublishToLatestPublished is listed as a CloudFormation-only directive with no SDK equivalent
sources.note: Read in the bundled JavaScript of the npm package (deploy-engine and program chunks), not in the GitHub source tree.

sources.title: Tag propagation
supports: PropagateTags applies up to 40 tags to the instances, EBS volumes, and network interfaces that Lambda creates, for cost allocation

sources.title: Node.js v24: Asynchronous context tracking
supports: AsyncLocalStorage is stable; run(store, callback) makes the store available to everything called inside the callback, across asynchronous operations, and getStore() returns undefined outside of it

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: How Workers works (last updated 2026-09-18)
supports: A single Workers instance may handle multiple requests, including concurrent requests, in a single-threaded event loop
Cloudflare recommends not using or mutating global state, because requests may or may not share an instance and an isolate may be evicted

sources.title: Vercel: Fluid compute (last updated 2026-08-24)
supports: With Fluid compute multiple invocations share one function instance; optimized concurrency is available on the Node.js and Python runtimes
Fluid compute has been enabled by default for new projects since April 23, 2025
Multiple invocations can share the same physical instance (a global state/process) concurrently

sources.title: Vercel: Functions usage and pricing
supports: Fluid compute bills Active CPU, Provisioned Memory, and Invocations; after all requests complete the instance is paused and nothing is charged until the next invocation

definition.ja: Lambda の関数を、自分のアカウントの VPC にある EC2 インスタンスで動かす機能。インスタンスの起動、パッチ、ルーティング、スケーリングは Lambda が行い、料金はインスタンスの時間に対してかかる。
definition.en: The Lambda feature that runs functions on EC2 instances in a VPC of your own account. Lambda launches, patches, routes to, and scales the instances, and you pay for instance-hours.

glossary.ja: キャパシティプロバイダー（Lambda）

definition.ja: Lambda Managed Instances で、関数を動かすインスタンスの置き場所と条件を決めるリソース。サブネット、セキュリティグループ、オペレーターロール、インスタンスの種類、vCPU の上限を持つ。同じキャパシティプロバイダーに載せた関数は、互いに信頼できるものとして扱われる。
definition.en: In Lambda Managed Instances, the resource that says where and on what the functions run: subnets, security groups, an operator role, instance types, and a vCPU ceiling. Functions on the same capacity provider are treated as trusting one another.

definition.ja: Lambda が、キャパシティプロバイダーのインスタンスを起動し管理するために引き受ける IAM ロール。関数が動くときの実行ロールとは別のもの。
definition.en: The IAM role Lambda assumes to launch and manage the instances of a capacity provider. It is not the execution role a function runs as.

glossary.ja: マルチコンカレンシー

definition.ja: 1 つの実行環境が、同時に複数のリクエストを処理すること。標準の Lambda は 1 つの実行環境で一度に 1 つしか処理しない。
definition.en: One execution environment handling several requests at the same time. Standard Lambda handles one at a time per execution environment.

note.ja: 8 ファイル、52 件。同時に処理中の 2 つのリクエストでリクエスト ID が入れ替わること（モジュールスコープ）と入れ替わらないこと（AsyncLocalStorage）を、関数の呼び出しと本物のソケットの両方で決まった順序で再現。ワーカースレッド 2 本で Map が別々になること。設定の検証、ログへの経路のモデル、料金の入力、損益分岐の計算、スタックのアサーション
note.en: 8 files, 52 tests. Two requests in flight swapping request IDs with module scope and not with AsyncLocalStorage, replayed in a fixed order both as function calls and over real sockets. Two worker threads each holding their own Map. Settings validation, the model of the path to CloudWatch Logs, pricing inputs, the break-even arithmetic, and stack assertions

summary.ja: 35章のスタックを AWS に一度もデプロイしていない。cdkd 0.296.28 が `AWS::Lambda::CapacityProvider` と、`CapacityProviderConfig` を持つ `AWS::Lambda::Function` を Cloud Control API 経由で作れること、`$LATEST.PUBLISHED` が自動で公開されること、API Gateway が修飾子なしの関数を呼べること、デプロイする IAM identity に `lambda:PassCapacityProvider` と `iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole` が要ることが未確認。
summary.en: The chapter 35 stack has never been deployed. Unverified: that cdkd 0.296.28 creates `AWS::Lambda::CapacityProvider` and an `AWS::Lambda::Function` with `CapacityProviderConfig` through Cloud Control API, that `$LATEST.PUBLISHED` is published automatically, that API Gateway can invoke the unqualified function, and that the deploying identity needs `lambda:PassCapacityProvider` and `iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole`.

resume.ja: `vp run net:infra:deploy -c interfaceEndpoints=logs` の後に `vp run lmi:infra:deploy`、`vp run lmi:smoke`、`vp run lmi:infra:drift` を通す。終わったら `vp run lmi:infra:destroy`、`vp run net:infra:destroy` の順に消す（時間課金。1 日でおよそ USD 8.87）。
resume.en: After `vp run net:infra:deploy -c interfaceEndpoints=logs`, run `vp run lmi:infra:deploy`, `vp run lmi:smoke`, and `vp run lmi:infra:drift`. Then delete with `vp run lmi:infra:destroy` and `vp run net:infra:destroy`, in that order (hourly charges, about USD 8.87 a day).

summary.ja: インスタンスの台数、EBS ボリュームの大きさと料金、2 つの AZ のサブネットに 3 台がどう配置されるか、`minExecutionEnvironments` を 3 未満にしたときの台数を確認していない。料金の計算は「3 台」という仮定に立っている。
summary.en: Not confirmed: how many instances start, the size and price of their EBS volumes, how three instances are placed across subnets in two zones, and the count when `minExecutionEnvironments` is below 3. The cost figures rest on the assumption of three instances.

resume.ja: デプロイ後に、キャパシティプロバイダーのシステムログと CloudWatch のメトリクス（名前空間 `AWS/Lambda`、ディメンション `CapacityProviderName`）で台数を見る。EC2 の managed resource visibility を切り替えてインスタンスとボリュームを確かめ、数日後に請求の明細と突き合わせる。
resume.en: After a deploy, read the instance count from the capacity provider's system logs and CloudWatch metrics (namespace `AWS/Lambda`, dimension `CapacityProviderName`). Switch EC2's managed resource visibility to see the instances and volumes, and compare with the bill a few days later.

summary.ja: Lambda の実行環境で、同時実行、ワーカースレッドの数、スケーリング、スロットリング（429）、インスタンスの入れ替え、タイムアウト後もコードが動き続けることを一度も観測していない。手元のテストが再現しているのは、1 つの Node.js プロセスと、自分で起こした worker_threads だけ。
summary.en: Never observed on Lambda's own execution environment: concurrent invocations, the number of worker threads, scaling, throttling (429), instance replacement, and code that keeps running after a timeout. The local tests reproduce one Node.js process and worker_threads started by the test itself.

resume.ja: デプロイ後に `vp run lmi:smoke` を通し、負荷をかけて `ConcurrencyThrottles`、`CPUThrottles` と実行環境の数を見る。負荷試験は 32章の方針に従う。
resume.en: After a deploy, pass `vp run lmi:smoke`, then apply load and watch `ConcurrencyThrottles`, `CPUThrottles`, and the number of execution environments. Follow chapter 32 for load testing.

summary.ja: インスタンスが VPC から届く必要のある宛先を、CloudWatch Logs と X-Ray のほかに確認できていない。CloudWatch Logs のインターフェースエンドポイントだけのプライベートサブネットで関数のバージョンが ACTIVE になるかは未確認。
summary.en: Beyond CloudWatch Logs and X-Ray, the destinations the instances must reach from the VPC were not confirmed. Whether a function version becomes ACTIVE in private subnets with only the CloudWatch Logs interface endpoint is unverified.

resume.ja: 既定の構成でデプロイし、関数のバージョンが ACTIVE になるかを見る。ならなければ `vp run net:infra:deploy -c egress=nat` で試し、VPC Flow Logs で拒否された宛先を調べる。
resume.en: Deploy the default layout and see whether the function version becomes ACTIVE. If not, try `vp run net:infra:deploy -c egress=nat` and look up the refused destinations in VPC Flow Logs.
